claim: Thomas A. Carlson's paper "Defense First: A Multi-Asset Tactical Model for Adaptive Downside Protection" is a 2025 SSRN preprint (DOI 10.2139/ssrn.5334772); full text was not retrievable through fetch tooling, so this round pins exact rules from the AllocateSmartly/Quantitativo replications and the author's own LinkedIn summary, same as H-20260923-12.
quote: SSRN Electronic Journal. Published: 2025-01-01. Preprint. 0 citations.
limitations: Only a short bibliographic stub renders (509 bytes); abstract/full text not retrievable. Reused unchanged from H-20260923-12 (dir:defense_first_taa_carlson_concretum, dir:s3_defense_first_remainder) -- not re-fetched, per the research-mission rule to reuse already-verified sources rather than duplicate the same fetch.
independent_replication: Cross-checked by two independent replications used below: AllocateSmartly (tested from 1971) and Quantitativo; both state the same asset menu and tiered-weight mechanism.
impact_on_spec: Confirms the paper exists and is a preprint (practitioner/preprint credibility tier, not peer-reviewed); D1's exact rules are sourced from the AllocateSmartly/LinkedIn cards below, not this primary listing.

claim: AllocateSmartly's independent replication of Carlson's Defense First states momentum for TLT/GLD/(PDBC or DBC)/UUP plus BIL is measured monthly at the close as the average of each asset's 1, 3, 6 and 12-month dividend-adjusted percent return.
quote: Momentum is measured as the average of each asset’s 1, 3, 6 and 12-month dividend-adjusted % return.
limitations: Secondary source, not the primary PDF; AllocateSmartly substitutes PDBC where the author's LinkedIn post and Quantitativo say DBC -- this round uses DBC (matches local data, matches the author's own description). Reused unchanged from H-20260923-12.
independent_replication: Corroborated by Quantitativo's separate replication (same four-asset menu, same tiered-weight structure) and by the author's own LinkedIn confirmation of the DBC ticker.
impact_on_spec: D1's `weights_fn` computes this exact 1/3/6/12 calendar-month blended return, generalized to any signal date (not only the true month-end) so the batch harness's 21 rebalance-day offsets can each evaluate it without look-ahead -- offset 0 reproduces the true month-end reading used in H-20260923-12's DF01.

claim: AllocateSmartly states Defense First ranks the four defensive assets from highest to lowest momentum and assigns tiered weights 40% (top rank), 30%, 20%, 10% (bottom rank).
quote: Rank the four defensive assets from highest to lowest momentum, with portfolio allocation to each as follows: 40% (top rank), 30%, 20% and 10%.
limitations: Same secondary-source caveat as the momentum-definition card. Reused unchanged from H-20260923-12.
independent_replication: Weights independently confirmed by Quantitativo's replication and the registry's dir:defense_first_taa_carlson_concretum harvest, both stating the same 40/30/20/10 tiering.
impact_on_spec: Pins D1's exact rank-to-weight table (40/30/20/10, RANK_WEIGHTS in run_h20260923_12_s3_defense_first.py, reused unedited) -- not tuned, not searched.

claim: AllocateSmartly states that if a defensive asset's momentum is less than that of T-bills (BIL), Defense First allocates that asset's tier weight to US stocks (SPY) instead -- an absolute-momentum screen applied per asset per tier every month.
quote: If a defensive asset’s momentum is less than that of T-bills, allocate that portion of the portfolio to US stocks (SPY).
limitations: Same secondary-source caveat. Reused unchanged from H-20260923-12.
independent_replication: Same hurdle/fallback structure described in Quantitativo's replication and the author's own LinkedIn post.
impact_on_spec: D1 is preregistered as the paper's own published rule -- failing tier goes to SPY (the 'original rules' reading the queue task asked for), distinct from H-20260923-12's DF02 variant which redirected the failing tier to SHY instead; D1 in this round does not use that departure.

claim: AllocateSmartly states Defense First holds all positions until the end of the following month and rebalances monthly regardless of whether the target allocation has changed.
quote: Hold all positions until the end of the following month. Rebalance monthly regardless of whether there is a change in position.
limitations: No explicit close-vs-next-open fill lag stated in the source; this repo's frozen contract (close signal, next-open fill) is applied on top, disclosed as an addition. Reused unchanged from H-20260923-12.
independent_replication: Consistent with every other monthly TAA rule this repo has implemented (S2, S3, H-20260923-12).
impact_on_spec: Pins D1 to unconditional monthly rebalancing (every month-end signal date, all 21 offsets), matching the batch harness's own monthly-offset convention.

claim: Thomas Carlson's own LinkedIn announcement states the model allocates monthly across four liquid macro-hedging ETFs (TLT, GLD, DBC, UUP) using multi-horizon momentum and an absolute strength filter, with SPY as a fallback asset.
quote: The model allocates monthly across four liquid, macro-hedging ETFs (TLT, GLD, DBC, UUP), using multi-horizon momentum and an absolute strength filter, with SPY as a fallback asset.
limitations: Promotional social-media post, not the paper itself. Reused unchanged from H-20260923-12.
independent_replication: Confirms the DBC ticker (not AllocateSmartly's PDBC substitute) against Quantitativo's independent replication.
impact_on_spec: Deciding source for D1's universe using DBC (available locally, 2016-01-04..2026-09-25) rather than PDBC.

claim: Quantitativo's independent backtest replication of Carlson's Defense First reports that, at roughly the S&P 500's own volatility, a 3x-leveraged-fallback variant delivers materially higher CAGR (16.2% vs 10.6%) with a better Sharpe and much smaller drawdowns than SPY buy-and-hold.
quote: With roughly the same level of volatility as the S&P 500, the strategy now delivers significantly higher returns (16.2% vs. 10.6%) while maintaining a superior Sharpe ratio and much smaller drawdowns.
limitations: The 16.2%/10.6% figures are Quantitativo's own leveraged-fallback extension, not the paper's unleveraged base case (10.4% per the registry's harvest). Reused unchanged from H-20260923-12; not used for D1's exact rule text (AllocateSmartly is used for that), only for triangulating that three independent parties (Quantitativo, AllocateSmartly, BestFolio per the registry) replicate a real, non-single-blogger mechanism.
independent_replication: One of three independent replications (Quantitativo, AllocateSmartly, and BestFolio per dir:defense_first_taa_carlson_concretum) of the same published mechanism.
impact_on_spec: Supports existing_solution_comparison in direction-review.json: the mechanism is a real, multiply-replicated published rule, not a single unverified blog post.

claim: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen (2012, Journal of Financial Economics) document time-series momentum: an asset's own trailing 12-month excess return positively predicts its own future return, and this holds for every one of 58 diverse futures/forward contracts (equity indices, currencies, commodities, sovereign bonds) they examine over 25+ years.
quote: 12-month time series momentum profits are positive not just on average across these assets, but for every asset contract we examine.
limitations: Evidence is on liquid futures/forward contracts (58 instruments), not the specific TLT/GLD/DBC/UUP ETF basket, and not long-only cash-hurdle-screened weights; it motivates D1/D2's mechanism (own-asset trailing-return momentum) but is not itself evidence either candidate clears this repo's 10/20bp cost contract or combines well with S3.
independent_replication: Peer-reviewed, published in Journal of Financial Economics (2012); the mechanism (time-series/absolute momentum) is the same one Carlson's Defense First and this round's D2 both apply to a defensive four-ETF basket, and the same one AQR's own follow-on century study (below) re-tests over a much longer sample.
impact_on_spec: Grounds D2's rule (hold an asset only when its own trailing 12-month return beats cash-proxy SHY, size by inverse realized vol) as an application of a peer-reviewed, independently-documented anomaly rather than a home-grown rule; D2's specific thresholds (12-month lookback, 63-session vol, SHY hurdle) are the round numbers the queue task specifies, not tuned to this paper's own parameters.

claim: Hurst, Ooi and Pedersen (2017, Journal of Portfolio Management) extend time-series-momentum/trend-following evidence back to 1880 using a novel data set, finding the strategy was consistently profitable across the following ~110 years and performed well in 8 of the 10 largest historical crisis periods, with low correlation to traditional stock/bond benchmarks.
quote: the strategy was consistently profitable over the next 110 years
limitations: Broad multi-asset futures trend evidence over a century, not this repo's specific defensive ETF basket, cost contract, or combination-with-S3 question; the paper itself flags rising correlations across markets and increased assets in the strategy since the credit crisis as headwinds, a caution this round's stress-period (2016-2023) and 2022-correlation reporting are designed to surface locally.
independent_replication: Published in Journal of Portfolio Management (2017); extends and corroborates Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen (2012) over a ~9x longer sample using an independently constructed historical data set.
impact_on_spec: Motivates evaluating D1/D2 across the full stress period (2016-05..2023-09, including the 2018Q4 and 2020 and 2022 drawdowns) and reporting 2022-specific correlation with S3, rather than relying on the anchor window alone; also grounds the round's explicit caution that trend-following's edge can compress as correlations rise, which is exactly the diversifier-edge test (K2) checks for the S3 combination.
